title.narrative: COVID-19: Active Response and Expenditure Support Program

description.narrative: The CARES program provides budgetary support to meet the development financing needs arising from the government's countercyclical pandemic response measures. The program is aligned with the following impact: adverse impacts of COVID-19 on the population's health, incomes, and economic opportunities as well as macroeconomic stability mitigated. The effect of the reforms is the COVID-19 outbreak more effectively managed and its adverse social and economic impacts reduced. The program has three outputs: (i) the COVID-19 response and health system strengthening measures implemented; (ii) social protection for the poor households expanded; and (iii) affected sectors supported to prevent job losses from the economic downturn. The program is aligned with the ADB's country partnership strategy, 2017-2021 for Afghanistan and the government's development strategy under the Afghanistan National Peace and Development Frameworks (ANPDF I and draft ANPDF II) and Self-Reliance for Mutual Accountability Framework.

Malnutrition among children under 5 years of age maintained at or below 41% and among women maintained at or below 20% Progress/Status: Data being collected and/or not yet published. Malnutrition can be divided into two subgroups, stunting, and wasting. Stunting is associated with lack of access to adequate food over the long run and poverty, particularly the first 1000 days of child life, while wasting represents lack of access to food in the short run. Proportion of stunting is measured by percentage of children aged 0-59 months who are below minus two standard deviations from median height-for-age of the WHO Child Growth Standards. The 2018 National Health Survey reveals that the national stunting rate for children under five is 36.6%, where its severe form is 17.3%. The national wasting rate is 5%, and its severe form is 1.5%. According to UNICEF data before the pandemic, Afghanistan has one of the world's highest rates of stunting in children under five at about 40% (upper bound). The rate of wasting in Afghanistan is extremely high at 9.5%. One in three adolescent girls suffers from anaemia. Only half of Afghan babies are exclusively breastfed in their first six months. Only 12% of Afghan children aged 6-24 months receive the right variety of food in the quantity needed for their age.9 Based on UNICEF/WHO/World Bank estimates in Table below, the proportion of stunting is expected to remain stable, however the 2020 estimates do not account for the full impact of COVID-19. Household survey data on child height and age were not collected in 2020 due to physical distancing policies. One of the covariates used in the country model takes the impact of COVID-19 partially into account. Thus full information about the change in rate of malnutrition among the children is not yet available. Latest estimates on the change in women's malnutrition is also not yet available. Data Source: UNICEF and World Bank country reports Actual value:

National poverty rate maintained at or below 61% Progress/Status: Target achieved. Based on the latest Integrated Expenditure and Labor Force Survey under the World Bank report, poverty declined from 54.5% in 2017 to 47.1% in 2020. Rural poverty declined from 59.0% in 2017 to 47.6% in 2020, mainly reflecting expanded agricultural output after recovery from the 2018 drought. Urban poverty, on the other hand, has reached a new high of 45.5% in 2020 (up from 41.6% in 2017), reflecting weakness in service and industry sectors, and the negative impacts of COVID-19 lockdowns and disruptions. Increases in poverty were most pronounced among households dependent on self-employment and casual employment in services and manufacturing, including daily laborers and small-scale retailers. The high number of returnees and internally displaced persons is placing pressure on limited services and employment opportunities in urban centers. The changes in poverty rate will be monitored continuously in 2021. Data Source: Quarterly reports from the MOF and World Bank country reports Actual value:

Daily number of COVID-19 confirmed cases reduced to not more than 50 Progress/Status: Target partly achieved. According to WHO data, until end March 2021, Afghanistan was able to reduce the daily number of COVID-19 confirmed cases below 50. On 15 January 2021, number of daily cases were 56, on 15 February 2021, daily cases were 22, and on 14 March 2021, daily cases were 26 cases. However, since end April 2021, there is an increase in number of daily confirmed cases. As of 20 May 2021, daily confirmed cases reached 453. It is also important to note that the number of confirmed cases is lower than the number of actual cases because of limited testing in Afghanistan. Given the Afghan government's plan for vaccinating 60% of the Afghan population during the ongoing year, the DMF target is achievable if the available vaccine proved effective against the COVID-19's new variants. Data Source: Reports from the MOPH; WHO country reports and Data on daily country updates on COVID-19 from https://ourworldindata.org/ Actual value:

Output: COVID-19 response and health system strengthening measures implemented Indicator: At least 500 ventilators, 100,000 testing kits, and appropriately sized personal protective gear, including gender-responsive individual packages for female health workers delivered and gender-sensitive treatment areas established at identified medical facilities Achievement: 600 Progress/Status: Target achieved. According to the MOPH's COVID-19 Coordinator, since the beginning of the pandemic, Afghanistan emerged from having no COVID-19 testing labs in the country to establishing 22 specialized laboratories with more than 250,000 testing kits in stock and a national capacity of 8,500 tests per day. As of April 2021, 361,751 people have been tested for COVID-19 compared to 133,691 tests as of end November 2020. Afghanistan has 750 oxygen concentrators and 600 ventilators in use and trained health care staff to operate them. Afghanistan was able to obtain four GeneXpert devices of them, which can turn around COVID-19 test results in a matter of 45 minutes. With support from development partners such as WHO, World Bank, UNICEF and bilateral donors, personal protective equipment were provided to health workers nationwide. Healthcare providers including female staff have obtained protective gear and specialized areas for gender-sensitive treatment. Afghanistan started producing mask and personal protection gears locally. Data Source: COVID-19 response reports from the MOPH and WHO country reports

Output: Social protection for the poor households expanded Indicator: At least 310,000 households below the poverty line received daily bread assistance, with priority given to women-headed households, targeted at 10% of total households Progress/Status: Target achieved for Kabul Municipality and data being collected and/or not yet published for other provinces. A bread distribution program was launched in all provinces in May 2020 and implemented by the local governments and municipalities. According to the implementation plan, district and village-level monitoring committees were formed to identify people in need, particularly the women-headed households and supervise the distribution through local bakeries. According to Kabul Municipality, 311,320 households received bread assistance. CARES Program monitoring and evaluation specialist obtained the spreadsheet for bread distribution program from Kabul Municipality, which requires additional data analysis for gender disaggregation. However, data on bread distribution at the provincial level from IDLG is not yet available to illustrate the exact number of beneficiaries at the national level. Similarly, the exact percentage for women beneficiaries is not yet available. However, given the Afghan population composition, the female to male ratio is roughly equal, therefore, half of the beneficiaries would be women. In addition to the bread distribution program, the government also procured wheat flour and distributed to the bakeries in Kabul. Each bakery received 30 sacks of wheat flour. Out of 30 sacks, 20 bags were turned into bread, distributed later in a day to needy. The remaining ten bags paid for the cost of bakery service. This intervention put bread on needy people's tables and controlled wheat flour price inflation successfully. Data Source: Quarterly reports from the MOF, reports from the Kabul city municipality, and World Bank country reports Actual value:

Output: Social protection for the poor households expanded Indicator: Water and electricity bill up to AF1,000 covered by the local government for 2 months for at least 350,000 households in Kabul, with priority given to women-headed households, targeted at 10% of total households Progress/Status: Not achieved. According to the power utility company, Da Afghanistan Breshna Sherkat (DABS) database, the actual numbers of beneficiaries are lower than the initial forecast. 293,666 households were exempted from electricity bills. Given population composition, half of the beneficiaries are believed to be women. However, when it comes to households exempted from the bill, only 3.4% are headed by women. Going through the electricity and water exemption list, several shops, including food stores and pharmacies, attached to residential houses were also exempted from the electricity bills. Output: Affected sectors supported to prevent job losses from the economic downturn Indicator: Da Afghanistan Bank reduced loan loss provisioning requirements to maintain MSME lending with ACGF guarantees-total bank lending ratio of at least 17% Progress/Status: Data being collected and/or not yet published. DAB has developed a post COVID-19 improvement plan for the banking sector to apply from July 2020 to December 2021. The plan envisages unwinding remaining emergency measures (from July 2020 onwards) contingent on further normalization; expanding electronic, mobile, and branchless banking; supporting credit recovery, focusing on MSMEs, including through partial credit guarantees from the Afghanistan Credit Guarantee Fund; and reducing banks' operating costs and suspending dividend payments for all banks for the rest of 2020. The World Bank-funded capitalization of the Credit Guarantee Fund is expected to provide partial credit guarantee for MSME loans. Earlier DAB reduced loan loss provisioning requirements for loans that are covered by risk guarantees from the ACGF to sustain lending to the private sector. World Bank's $100 million grant for Strengthening Afghanistan's Financial Intermediation (SAFI) Project is geared towards improving access to finance interventions (i.e. though credit guarantees and recovery grants for MSMEs coping with COVID-19) and strengthening of institutional capacity of DAB to manage the impact of the economic slowdown on financial sector stability. The project supports: i) capital contribution to ACGF enabling scaling up partial credit guarantees to participating financial institutions to increase lending to MSMEs; ii) matching grants program to MSMEs for their businesses; iii) development of legal and regulatory framework for deposit insurance, related capacity building, and capital contribution to the deposit insurance fund; iv) modernization of DAB's information technology infrastructure; and v) institutional capacity for DAB's financial system regulation and oversight. The information on number of newly disbursed MSME loans guaranteed by ACGF is yet to be collected in coordination with the World Bank. On 1 October 2020, the High Economic Council of Afghanistan approved a 2-year MSME support package for $294.8 million, with $200.0 million to be provided in 2021 and the remainder in 2022. In early 2021, DAB in collaboration with Ministry of Commerce and Industry prepared a draft proposal on “SME Support Procedure.” An Incentive Package Support Committee, chaired by the DAB Governor is envisaged, comprising deputy ministers and their equivalents from Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Industry and Commerce, Ministry of Agriculture, Kabul Municipality, Independent Directorate of Local Governance and DABs along with the representatives of the development partners and federation of chambers. The proposed MSME support measures include tax incentives, exemptions of municipal fees or rent payments for government-owned properties, reductions or exemptions in electricity bill payments, establishment of first-loss fund at DAB for allocation of first loss guarantees across banks and reviewing individual loans to MSMEs and monitoring losses. The proposed procedures include fees for the first-loss fund, loan-loss reimbursement procedure, eligibility criteria for loan applications and related monitoring arrangements for the first loss fund. Since the mechanism is yet to be established, no information has been released regarding the MSME support package as of date. Information will be collected in coordination with the DAB and relevant ministries for the next quarterly reports. Data Source: Quarterly reports from the MOF, reports from the Da Afghanistan Bank, Ministry of Economy and World Bank country reports Actual value:

Output: Affected sectors supported to prevent job losses from the economic downturn Indicator: At least 60,000 permanent agriculture sector jobs, of which at least 30% are provided to women, generated as a result of sector-specific incentives Progress/Status: Target partly achieved. The Ministry of Agriculture, Irrigation and Livestock has supported processing and packaging units and cold storage at the rural community level under the government's Afghanistan Crop Management Project to prevent wastage of high-value perishable fresh fruit and vegetables that could not be exported. Creating jobs in the agriculture sector supported Afghans' livelihoods in a difficult time. According to the Ministry of Agriculture and President's Office, as of April 2021, 71,209 people got jobs directly and 103,314 people indirectly. Data on gender composition of the job generated is not yet available. Data Source: Quarterly reports from the MOF, reports from the Ministry of Agriculture, Irrigation and Livestock and World Bank country reports Actual value:

Output: COVID-19 response and health system strengthening measures implemented Indicator: All actions related to surveillance and early detection; case management; infection prevention and control; risk communication, and coordination in the COVID-19 National Emergency Response Plan completed Achievement: Y Progress/Status: The National Emergency Response Plan (NERP) for COVID-19 was approved by MOPH in March 2020 and a new structure within the MOPH was created to implement the NERP and the national action plan. The NERP details the medium and long-term strategy for a robust national health security agenda for all hazards and pandemic preparedness, as well as the resource requirements and development coordination for (i) surveillance and detection; (ii) early diagnosis, isolation, and case management; (iii) infection prevention and control in health facilities and communities; (iv) risk mitigation; and (v) resource allocation for logistics and procurement for emergency responses based on the COVID-19 preparedness and response plans of the WHO and the UNICEF. The MOPH maintains a resource map covering the availability of medical equipment, medicines, personal protective equipment, etc. for all its health facilities, which is used for matching available resources at the health facilities with needs of the pandemic. According to the MOPH's COVID-19 Coordinator, MOPH has been proactive in preparedness and early response to the COVID-19 pandemic and strengthening the readiness and capacity of the medical facilities, including emergency procurement of medical supplies and equipment. The MOPH was projecting, if preventative measures are not taken, 80% of the population could be infected, and mortality might have reached up to 125,000 deaths alone in Kabul. The first case of COVID-19 in Afghanistan was reported on 23 February 2020, when 150,000 Afghans returned from Iran to Afghanistan, Herat city. According to WHO, Afghanistan was among the first countries to consider multispectral and proactive preparedness measures in managing the COVID-19 outbreak, despite its fragile health system and surveillance capacities. One of the earliest detection measures was crossborder screening at entry points due to the surge of returnees from Iran, known as the hot spot for COVID-19 at that time. This was followed by a Presidential decree forbidding crowds and up scaling hand hygiene. The Ministry of Interior Affairs banned large gatherings and sporting events. In March 2020, MOPH, together with the WHO, developed National Emergency Response Plan for COVID-19. The government increased the allocation of budget resources for health measures to combat the COVID-19 pandemic. The government brought required coordination and collaboration between media and religious leaders to soften panic in the communities and combatting misinformation. The MOPH and Ministry of Communication and Technology Affairs jointly developed a mobile application providing updates on COVID-19. The WHO emergency team launched a media campaign by holding a month-long roundtables discussion about the subject and oriented 55,256 communities and religious leaders in 34 provinces. Educational materials were developed, and the Ministry of Religious Affairs declared a fatwa regarding preventive measures. MOPH designated 8 hospitals with specialized wards for exclusive treatment of the COVID-19 patients. Gender-sensitive isolation wards were identified for COVID-19 patients in all provinces. The MOPH designated the Afghan Japan hospital in Kabul as immediate COVID-19 treatment facilities. A 100-bed COVID-19 hospital was opened in Herat province. In Kabul, the Darulaman Palace (300 beds) as well as Kabul and Polytechnic universities' dormitories were converted to isolation facilities. MOPH prepared 10 additional 50-bed medical facilities in Herat, Farrah, Neemruz and Kabul. Development partners, including ADB have been supporting MOPH to rehabilitate and expand new treatment facilities including prefabricated ones. As of 20 May 2021, 5,286 beds are available, of which 440 are intensive care unit beds. COVID-19 Projections by the Institute of Health Metrics and Evaluation estimates that Afghanistan needs 1,091 intensive care unit beds. Data Source: COVID-19 response reports from the MOPH and WHO country reports Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2021 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: COVID-19 response and health system strengthening measures implemented Indicator: Gender-sensitive public awareness campaign on COVID-19 rolled out by MOPH and Ministry of Women Affairs to reach people across 34 provinces Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Target achieved. According to the MOPH's COVID-19 Coordinator, a nationwide gender-sensitive public awareness campaign on COVID-19 has been carried out by the MOPH and other agencies. Depending on the mandate of the agency, some agencies were mainstreaming gender explicitly. Using mosques, educational institutions as well as national print and broadcasting media, social media, billboards, cell phone messages, COVID-19 related informational documents have been distributed using visual graphics for both sexes and ages. Population has been sensitized about hygiene promotion through handwashing stations and distribution of hygiene kits. A call center was set up at MOPH to share information with the public. MOPH designated special treatment wards for female patients in the hospital. MoPH provided guidance/protocols for affected pregnant and lactating women. MOPH was among the first agencies to redesign its database to allow gender analysis. Ministry of Women Affairs has been involved in 117 districts in 26 provinces by (i) visiting women jails, safe homes, shelters, businesses headed by women, orphanages, private banks, hospitals, and clinics to distribute gender-sensitive information and sanitary kits, (ii) monitoring adherence to safety measures, and (iii) facilitating gender-sensitive services for women, particularly in hospitals with all women-only treatment facilities. Health kits for street children have been distributed. The United Nations Population Funds, United Nations Development Program, and Ministry of Women Affairs also addressed the violence against women during the pandemic. The government has prioritized women-headed households for its social protection schemes (retirement, refugees and returnees, and war victim). Data Source: COVID-19 response reports from the MOPH and WHO country reports Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2021 Target value: Y Actual value: Y
